target_customer: At YC time: aspiring tech workers choosing coding bootcamps, paid by bootcamps per enrolled student. Now: enterprises in education, insurance and travel buying AI outbound agents.
problem: Career Karma helped people choosing a coding bootcamp find the right school and get career support; OutRival (2024) replaces human outbound calls, texts and emails with AI agents for enterprises.
business_model: Career Karma: marketplace fees from bootcamps and schools. OutRival: B2B subscription and usage fees for AI digital workers.
product_category: Career education marketplace, then enterprise conversational AI agents

founders.name: Ruben Harris
founders.background_notes: Per YC page and company site. An interview transcript snippet suggests a sales background but I did not open it. Education not found.

founders.name: Timur Meyster
founders.background_notes: Per YC page and company site; the two hosted Breaking Into Startups.

exit.reason: The Career Karma platform was acquired by Climb Credit in 2025-09, but the YC listed company OutRival is active.

competitors.name: Course Report
competitors.what: Bootcamp review and research site covering US and Canada providers
competitors.traction_then: a 2018 Course Report study counted 108 bootcamp providers in the US and Canada, cited by Axios

technical_complexity.rationale: Career Karma was a matching app and community with ordinary web engineering; the later AI agent product is harder but was not the product at founding.

defensibility.rationale: School directories and review content were copyable; the community and school data gave some stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals did not absorb the model; Career Karma grew, raised a 40 million Series B in 2022, laid off staff in 2022 and 2023 and was sold to Climb Credit in September 2025.

market_need_then: Coding bootcamp enrollment was growing in 2018 and prospective students had trouble choosing among 108 providers per a 2018 Course Report figure cited by Axios.

branding.domain_note: Career Karma used careerkarma.com; OutRival uses outrival.com; history not found

identity.voice_and_tone: OutRival: warm, mission driven, with lines such as Caring is the input, performance is the output

branding.brand_signature: Founders' Breaking Into Startups podcast audience

rebrands.why: OutRival launched in October 2024 as a new AI agent product from the Career Karma founders; Career Karma continued as a separate brand until sold

branding.community_and_virality: Career Karma built a community of more than 150,000 members per press coverage; founders hosted a startup podcast

brand_strength.rationale: Career Karma was a well covered consumer education brand with a large community; OutRival is a new B2B name with little brand evidence.

pivots.from: Career Karma, bootcamp matching and career coaching marketplace
pivots.to: OutRival, AI outbound agents for enterprises
pivots.why: TechCrunch says the founders launched OutRival after two years in beta; the YC page says they pivoted in 2024

outcome_analysis: The YC Winter 2019 company was Career Karma, which raised a 10 million Series A in December 2020 and a 40 million Series B in January 2022, cut staff in July 2022 and January 2023 and was sold to Climb Credit in September 2025. The same founders launched OutRival in October 2024 using leftover Career Karma capital, with insurance and travel verticals in 2026. Whether the pivot succeeds is not yet clear.
notes: The pages for these URLs other than TechCrunch, OutRival and YC were seen only as search results, not opened. Series A date and investor come from the search summary of press coverage. Total raised varies by source (51.9M vs 91.9M per Crunchbase quoted in coverage); any seed rounds are not recorded and may be missing. OutRival says it has raised a Series B per search snippets of press releases but the amount and date were not found, so no round recorded; careers page lists SoftBank, Initialized, Kapor and Imaginable Futures. The TechCrunch article states OutRival uses leftover Career Karma Series B capital. Layoffs: TechCrunch July 2022 and January 2023, about 60 and 22 per Built In. Competitor list is thin and the Axios date is not shown; source predates or is near the batch only because of the 2018 report it cites. The listed YC company page describes OutRival, not Career Karma, so the founding year and description come from different eras.
